features.name: share_comments_explaining_relevance
features.definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments explicitly explain why their point is relevant to the OP's view (e.g., 'which is why', 'this is why')?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments). For each comment, decide whether the commenter's own assertion explicitly explains why their point matters or is relevant to the OP's claim (title/argument give context for the target), e.g. connective explanations such as 'which is why' or 'this is why' that link a point to the OP's view, or equivalent explicit relevance-linking statements. Do not count mere quoted text from others unless adopted by the commenter. Ignore OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates and reports of the outcome; generic platform/delta-rule discussion is eligible but is not itself relevance explanation. Return number of qualifying comments divided by total comments (0 to 1). Empty list -> null; missing or malformed OC_comments -> null.

h0: share_comments_explaining_relevance has no association with delta.
h1: Higher share_comments_explaining_relevance is associated with higher probability of delta.
note: Operational assumption: 'counter-arguments' are the OC_comments; persuasiveness is the dataset outcome delta; the exposure is a row-level share of comments (an any-comment version would be a different measurement). Relevance explanation is judged semantically, not by literal phrase matching; the example phrases are illustrative. Comment order/timing unknown; comments may contain quotes or outcome text, which the prompt is told to exclude. Association only, not causal.
